description: Committee recommends new rules for horse-drawn carriages in Traffic Bylaw.

chips.text: Recommended
Establishes a new regulatory framework for horse-drawn vehicle businesses.

description: Pilot project removes 13 of 14 Central Avenue pay stations.
One pay station remains for non-digital payments.
Updates traffic bylaw to recognize modern payment methods.

chips.text: Recommended
Pilot project has $2,000 signage costs, funded by existing budget.
Councillor Pierce questioned accessibility for those without smartphones or apps.
Customers preferring cash or debit, or without smartphones, are impacted.
Pilot will inform future city-wide parking operations and digital payment decisions.
Councillor Pierce opposed, citing concerns for non-app users' access to parking.

description: Raise traffic fines for disobeying signs, obstructing intersections to $180.
Increase fines for splashing pedestrians, driving over lines to $75.
Adjust on-street loading zone fees to $360 for cost recovery.

chips.text: Recommended
A $20,000 annual funding shortfall exists for accessible parking zones.
Councillor Pears called the proposed residential accessible parking fee 'punitive'.
Commercial businesses, hotels, and churches using loading zones.
Resident Karen Kobussen opposed charging for residential accessible parking.
Proposed fees for accessible parking could dissuade people with disabilities from applying.
Administration will consult the Accessibility Advisory Committee on accessible parking fees.

speakers.name: Karen Kobussen
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Transportation Fines, Fees and Permits - October 2026 update
said: Charging residents $360 for accessible parking stalls is punitive.
This fee will dissuade people with mobility issues from applying.
City should consult accessibility groups before implementing this fee.

description: Committee recommends 51st Street/Millar Avenue pedestrian and cyclist upgrades.
Also recommends connecting rail warning system at 51st Street.

chips.text: Recommended
City's share for rail warning system interconnection is $810,000.
Councillor Donauer expressed concern about impacts on businesses and residents.
Small businesses on Miller Avenue face reduced access and revenue.
Committee rejected staff's Option C recommendation for full reconstruction.
No traffic forecast for 51st Street and Cleveland Avenue intersection.
Businesses strongly opposed Option C due to loss of access and revenue.
51st Street and Cleveland Avenue will be monitored for future signalization.

speakers.name: Jarvis Rein
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Millar Ave
said: Proposed median will substantially reduce traffic access to 30 small businesses.
Project addresses a problem occurring only one in a million times.
Option C will devalue properties, causing 25-30% revenue loss.

speakers.name: John Kearley
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 51st St and Millar Ave_redact
said: Only 0.00098% of vehicles are involved in accidents, so the issue is not broken.
Proposal will detrimentally affect 53 small businesses' ability to earn income and pay taxes.
Consultations were not genuine; council should vote against recommendations.

description: Committee recommends a 3-meter pathway on Millar Avenue's east side.
Also recommends a pathway and sidewalk for 43rd Street.

chips.text: Recommended
Estimated project cost is $9 million, currently unfunded.
Businesses and property owners along Miller Avenue are directly affected by parking impacts.
Committee amended staff's recommendation for pathways on both sides to only the east side.
No studies on bus ridership or cycling usage were presented for the proposed pathways.
Businesses largely preferred a single pathway on the east side of Miller Avenue to minimize impacts.
The project will require the removal of 157 trees, a reduction of 40 from the original plan.
Staff will provide City Council with a breakdown of parking impacts on the east versus west sides.

speakers.name: Jarvis Rein
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Millar Ave
said: Questions need for two paths on both sides of industrial road.
Compares to Warman Road, a residential area with one path.
Suggests using less busy side roads instead of Millar Avenue.

speakers.name: John Kearley
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 51st St and Millar Ave_redact
said: Questions $30 million cost for active transportation in industrial areas.
Asks why paths are on the busiest street in heavy industrial zone.
Wonders about estimated use and cost analysis, especially in winter.

speakers.name: Eugene Dupuis
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 51st Street and Millar Avenue
said: Right-of-way width varies; 25 meters is sufficient, not 30-40 meters.
Proposes reducing right-of-way from 43rd to 50th Street to 25 meters.
Would purchase excess right-of-way from city, not lease it.

speakers.name: Jae Malinowski
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Connecting Millar Avenue from 43rd Street to Marquis Drive
said: Would lose 100% of parking, devaluing his 50-year-old building.
Currently pays for a boulevard lease for customer/employee parking.
Supports an east side only path; no ridership/usage studies exist.

description: Saskatoon's 2025 winter road maintenance had a $3.03 million deficit.
Record 147 cm snowfall occurred, but service targets were met.
Future plans include snowplow upgrades and a road weather system.

chips.text: Total 2025 snow and ice management costs were $20.49 million.
Councillor Donauer asked if 2026 snow spending had already exceeded budget.
City will review and update the priority street network for transit link planning.

description: Saskatoon built 13 km sidewalks, 37 km cycling paths.
Updated bike bylaws and design standards for safer travel.
Secured $5.5 million in federal and provincial funding.

chips.text: Active Transportation Reserve started at $500,000 annually in 2014.
26,000+ children participated in Learn to Ride Safe program.
Policy sets standard for safe work zones for vulnerable road users.
Administration will present updated Active Transportation Plan later this fall/winter.
